summary: New Infectum cell is independently supported by konawḥi and gnawḥi; this realizes the inherited base nowəḥ without confusing nwḥ 1 (rest/die) with barking nwḥ 2.

MAC MuA Quzko/21 explicitly self-corrects crying koboxən to barking konawḥi. The cleaner verse 17 is selected instead; repeated identical tokens receive individual decisions without duplicate examples.
Preterit nwəḥḥe preserves the assimilated ḥ+l boundary, rather than introducing a different stem. Commands to a human and the performed barking are already inherited under Preterit/Imperativ.
Reconcile supplied PrS 42/62,69 with inherited prs 118/37,119/8–9 using a citation crosswalk; wording matches but the numbering systems should not be conflated.
Confirm the exact plural-agent suffix assimilation in nwəḥḥe (PrS 64/92) and the l-marked dog actor.

The barking target is marked by ʕal- (aʕle/aʕlayye); the plural actor can be an overt l-marked dog phrase with a Preterit L-agent. Human imitation of barking remains the same sense, not a figurative split.
